title: The Current of Devil's Throat
premise: Dominic Eastwick, a desert ranger who has spent a decade erasing himself from other people's lives, is hired to find a vanished government survey team in the Devil's Throat range. He discovers the team's leader alive — Elena Vasquez, the woman he once loved and abandoned when his duty to the service cost her everything — hiding because she uncovered that the survey was a cover for a mining consortium bribing officials to seize protected land. As snows close in and the glacier calving season opens the only pass for three days, Dominic must choose between delivering evidence that will destroy his own agency or protecting the man who has become like a brother to him: the corrupt director who once saved his life. In the end, Dominic crosses the throat with Elena, sends the evidence through anyway, and accepts exile — finding at last that belonging isn't a place you're assigned but a person you refuse to leave.
about_author: Orsen Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former backcountry surveyor who spent eleven years mapping remote ranges before turning to fiction. He writes from a cabin with no road access, which he insists is not a metaphor.

chapters.title: The Thief Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Tracking a petty thief across hardpan, Dominic loses the trail where no trail should end — the same signature as the missing survey team. His supervisor orders him to stand down; he goes anyway. Emotional beat: restless competence masking loneliness, the first crack in his chosen invisibility.

chapters.title: Gear Without Ghosts
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. He finds the survey camp intact — food cooked, beds made, radios silent — and one set of footprints leading into a slot canyon that dead-ends. Someone wanted to be unfound by people who know how to find. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: What the Canyon Keeps
chapters.summary: Elena's POV, interleaved with Dominic closing in. Elena reveals why she staged the disappearance: core samples proving the consortium's claims were falsified, and a director's signature she recognized. Emotional beat: fear braided with fury; she trusts the wilderness more than any institution.

chapters.title: The Face Across the Fire
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. He corners her at night and finds Elena Vasquez — the woman whose career he destroyed by following orders seven years ago. Neither draws a weapon; both want to. Emotional beat: old love curdling into accusation, then into reluctant alliance against the cold.

chapters.title: Ledger of Small Betrayals
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Moving toward the high pass, they trade confessions: his obedience, her ambition, the child she lost while he was on assignment. Meanwhile, Director Hale's search party enters the range behind them — officially a rescue. Emotional beat: grief becoming honesty, honesty becoming something warmer.

chapters.title: Hale's Long Shadow
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. The director who raised Dominic after his father's death knows exactly what the survey found — and what it would do to him. He orders the search turned inward, hunting Elena, and sends the one man who can track her: Dominic's protégé, Reyes. Emotional beat: corruption dressed as loyalty.

chapters.title: The Calving Season Opens
chapters.summary: Dominic and Elena's POV. The glacier groans awake; the pass through Devil's Throat will hold for roughly seventy-two hours. They race for it as Reyes appears on their flank — not hostile yet, but asking questions. Emotional beat: hope with a countdown attached.

chapters.title: Icefall
chapters.summary: All three POVs converge. A calving collapse strands Reyes with them; to save him, Dominic must reveal the evidence, forcing Reyes to choose between the mentor who made him and the institution that owns him. A second collapse takes their supplies. Emotional beat: loyalty tested under falling ice.

chapters.title: Devil's Throat
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, climax. Hale intercepts them at the pass mouth with a rescue helicopter and an ultimatum: hand over the samples or be left for the mountain. Dominic chooses — publicly, irrevocably — transmitting the evidence via the survey's buried relay and standing between Hale and Elena as the ice gives way beneath the chopper's landing skids. Emotional beat: love and duty finally pulling the same direction.

chapters.title: Where the Map Ends
chapters.summary: Elena's POV, resolution. Stripped of rank and license, Dominic walks out of the range with nothing but the clothes he wears — and Elena beside him. The consortium falls; Hale faces inquiry; Reyes testifies. On the far side of the mountains, Dominic stops being invisible on purpose. Emotional beat: quiet, earned belonging.
